source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Permitted UAP activities vary with state law or regulation and facility policy, so the nurse must know the rules in the current setting.","B":"UAP scope is established by one federal standard and therefore remains identical in every state, facility, and clinical practice environment.","C":"UAPs have unrestricted independent nursing scope because they are not licensed and therefore are not subject to delegation limitations.","D":"Delegation decisions depend only on the delegating nurse's personal judgment because state regulation and organizational policy do not apply."}}
source_row.rationale: Unlike RN licensure, which has some degree of standardization through mechanisms like the NCLEX and Nurse Licensure Compact, the scope of tasks permitted for unlicensed assistive personnel can vary by state regulation and individual facility policy, so nurses relocating to a new practice setting should familiarize themselves with the specific applicable regulations and policies to make appropriate, safe delegation decisions.
source_row.source_detail: NCSBN Delegation page and National Guidelines: jurisdictions have different laws/rules on delegation; licensed nurses must know what is permitted in their practice jurisdiction. Current NCSBN delegation guidance reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: NCSBN — UAP Scope of Practice Variation by State
source_row.stem: A nurse relocates to a different state and notes that the scope of tasks permitted for unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) differs somewhat from their previous state, though a new colleague assumes UAP scope must be federally standardized and identical everywhere.
